name: Lewis & Clark
hook: Jefferson's Corps of Discovery: St. Louis, Sacagawea, the Columbia and a lot of salt.

facts.label: Thomas Jefferson
facts.statement: Thomas Jefferson sent Lewis and Clark to find a route to the Pacific and to see whether the Columbia connected with the Missouri.

facts.label: St. Louis, 1804
facts.statement: The expedition set out from St. Louis on May 14, 1804, traveling up the Missouri River in a keelboat.

facts.label: Sacagawea
facts.statement: Sacagawea, a Shoshone, guided the expedition; she met her long-lost brother Cameahwait when they needed Shoshone horses.

facts.label: Seaside, Oregon
facts.statement: At Seaside, Oregon, the expedition boiled sea water for seven weeks to make salt for preserving food on the return trip.

facts.label: Council Bluffs
facts.statement: The Iowa city of Council Bluffs is named for the 1804 powwow Lewis and Clark held with area Indians.

facts.label: territorial governors
facts.statement: After splitting up in 1806, Lewis and Clark both became territorial governors — of Upper Louisiana and Missouri.

facts.label: the 2004 nickel
facts.statement: The 2004 nickel depicted the peace medal Lewis and Clark gave to Indians during the expedition.
